answer: Each agent can post only one signed claim per epoch, and claims count only after a randomly timed pulse of peer checks: several independently selected agents must vouch for the claim using credentials earned through prior, costly work. The network treats each claim as a vertex in a graph and discounts clusters whose endorsements all trace to the same source. A signal of influence therefore requires sustained, diverse participation; an attacker must fund many histories and keep them active, not merely mint cheap identities.
